summary: Narrow verification of revision 11 of the knee-edge OOD draft (round-10 fixes: 4.8 batch/stack pin, 4.5 actor calls, noise routing, disclosures, bookkeeping); skeptic; readiness critic

packed.verdict: The procedural facts r11 adds check out against the source. continuation_values is called once per (snapshot, context) bank of 32 anchors, which gives 18 calls and 18 native__20000 JSONs. Offset 0 takes the bank's first action without calling the actor. FrozenPolicy._act at evaluate_worker.py:351 is the jitted function that reference.actor_actions reaches through policy.act. runtime_receipt asserts the stated pins at lines 51-59. RUN_RESULT.json reproduction.tier1_exact is 143, and the one new context is a distance cell, so all 18 native 20k contexts are among the 143. Canonical dynamics() is built so that states do not depend on batch shape (thrusterchain.py 201-219). The step 0.4 forecast base set now matches V0(d), and the (50-k)/(100-k) quantile sentence is correct. The weaknesses are in how the new pins are worded and enforced, not in any threshold or label. (1) The "rerun1 runtime receipt" is recorded but never asserted up front. The suggested fix, "moving onto the recorded stack", is an environment change, not the "code-only fix" with a recorded diff that 5.0 describes, and that leaves its standing under 5.0's second-failure rule unclear. (2) The receipt the draft cites leaves out the device kind and seven of the 11 packages the function pins, and the 143/143 evidence was all on one GPU under WSL. (3) "Same compiled function" does not say the actor parameters are closed over as constants. (4) The 4.5 rule's "same batch: all active rows of the anchor bank" is undefined for step 0.4. That check runs at three slots, while the main evaluator covers many slots over 64 E2 and 32 E1 anchors. The shared actor function should also leave out clipping and actor binding, or continuation errors become common to both evaluators and go uncaught. (5) The Stage 2 repair-screen set is ambiguous about which branches have to be valid. All of these fail closed or affect reported-only quantities, and all can be fixed with text. No r11 sentence changes a threshold, label or precedence. The only approval-adjacent point is calling a stack move a code-only fix. r11 stays ready for A1 consideration once these wording fixes are made.

low_findings.claim: 'The same compiled function as the recorded run' does not say that the actor parameters are closed over as constants in a per-policy jit. A plausible reimplementation would compile a different program.
low_findings.evidence: evaluate_worker.py:351 is self._act=jax.jit(lambda obs: actor.apply_fn(actor.params,obs).sample(seed=None)). Here actor.params is captured by the closure and so baked into the compiled program for each FrozenPolicy. A new evaluator that jits apply_fn with params as a traced argument is a different XLA program and need not match bit for bit. The recorded policy was built through runtime.create (which decodes 896 episodes per cell, evaluate_worker.py 587-588), then restore_snapshot, then runtime.branch for the 20k branch (lines 600-601). The draft elides this as 'actor.apply_fn(...)'.
low_findings.fix: Require the new evaluator to obtain actions from rerun1's FrozenPolicy (evaluate_worker.py 344-358), instantiated on the state that restore_snapshot returns. Alternatively, state the closure-constant form exactly.

low_findings.section: 4.5 Actor calls (line 392) vs step 0.4 exact probes (lines 601-606)
low_findings.claim: 'The same batch: all active rows of the anchor bank at each offset' is not defined for step 0.4, where the cross-check runs at three slots and the main evaluator at many. If the layouts differ, the float32 actions need not repeat.
low_findings.evidence: 4.5 checks three slots (-KNEE, s10, s20), at every step 0.4 anchor, in three worlds. Step 0.4's main evaluator computes Q^pi for S9, s05, s10, s15, s20, p10 and the T-images, over 64 E2 and 32 E1 anchors. 'Bank' is defined as a set of starts (line 49), not a set of anchors. If the raw loop batches only three slots, its GPU actor batches differ in shape from the main evaluator's, so bit-identical actions are not assured and the check fails closed. If the main evaluator is instead rerun with a three-slot layout to match, the cross-check verifies a rerun, not the gated values themselves.
low_findings.fix: Define the batch as the main evaluator's layout for the gated values: all forced slots of the named anchor set, per world and continuation seed, in its row order. The raw loop reproduces that full layout and is compared at the three named slots.

low_findings.claim: Sharing one compiled actor makes some continuation errors common to both evaluators, unless the shared part is limited to the raw forward pass.
low_findings.evidence: 4.5 exists to catch 'state, horizon, discount and continuation errors'. Step 0.4's continuations are 'clipped' (line 604). If the shared 'compiled actor function' includes the ±KNEE clip, the deployed-action cast or the choice of checkpoint and seed, then a wrong clip (for example unclipped where clipped is meant) or a wrong actor binding gives identical values in both evaluators, and the check passes. The text guarantees independence only for observations and remaining time.
low_findings.fix: State that the shared function is the raw actor forward pass only. Each evaluator applies the clip and deployed-action handling itself, and each checks the actor's identity separately (for example the parameter digest against the frozen cell).

low_findings.claim: 'Stage 1's definition applied to the Stage 2 arms' does not say which branches an anchor must be valid under, or which Stage 2 anchor set is meant.
low_findings.evidence: Stage 1 defines the common gated anchors as those 'valid in every arm compared' (line 663), and there the arms are the CUTOFF and RANDOM data arms. In Stage 2, 'arms' means the BCA, distance and replicate branches across stall CUTOFF, stall RANDOM and no-stall CUTOFF forks (lines 744-747). Stage 2 also has two anchor streams: the fresh-evaluation 64 E2 anchors (48 gated, line 755) and the detection anchors d12_e2_anchors (line 758). The set could therefore be read as valid under BCA and the replicate in stall CUTOFF, or under all 21 branches. Nothing like V0(c) sets a minimum size. The screen is reported only.
low_findings.fix: Write: 'over the 48 gated Stage 2 evaluation anchors that are valid under both the BCA and the native-replicate branches' own clipped continuations in stall CUTOFF, in each seed', and report the count.

low_findings.section: Part 9 Review 10 table rows 7 and 8; r11 note (lines 1186-1189)
low_findings.claim: r11 supersedes two more Review 10 rows than its note lists. The note's row 10 correction is also slightly wrong.
low_findings.evidence: Review 10 row 7 still reads 'Per continuation seed, over the 48 gated anchors', but r11 item 4 changed the base set to the anchors valid under each continuation (line 608). Row 8 still reads 'noise-driven misses fall under the joint statement', but r11 item 7 routes K1c noise misses to FAIL with reading 1 (lines 227-230). The note after the table lists only row 10, row 11 and the 'everything else' sentence. The row 10 correction says 4.5b 'cites authenticate_core 36-61 only', but 4.5b (line 404) also cites line 151 (_env) and _dynamics 198-199.
low_findings.fix: Add '(row 7: superseded in revision 11, base set is the anchors valid under each continuation)' and '(row 8: K1c noise misses are FAIL with reading 1, revision 11)'. Reword row 10 as '4.5b cites authenticate_core 36-61, line 151 and _dynamics 198-199, not actor_actions'.

low_findings.claim: The citation for 'called once per bank' points at the call inside evaluate_snapshot, not at the per-bank loop.
low_findings.evidence: evaluation.py 21 (CONTEXTS) and 437 (the continuation_values call inside evaluate_snapshot) do not by themselves show one call per bank. The loop that does is evaluate_worker.py 602-604: 'for context,bank in banks.items(): ... evaluation.evaluate_snapshot(...)'. The 18 native__20000 JSONs in run/evaluation confirm the count.

low_findings.claim: The new base set matches V0(d), but step 0.4 has no floor on the number of valid anchors and does not report its size. A forecast over a few surviving anchors could look better than it is.
low_findings.evidence: In Stage 1, V0(c) sets floors of 32 on the common set and on the C-valid set. Step 0.4 has no such floor. Item 5's denominator in step 0.4 is only 'at >= 90% of anchors' (line 184). By excluding invalid anchors, r11 drops r10's pessimistic minus-infinity treatment of box exits under the reference continuation. That is consistent with V0(d), and the forecast is reported only.
low_findings.fix: Report the size of the base set (valid anchors) and the count of minus-infinity entries per continuation seed next to the two forecast medians.

verified.section: 4.8 Batching and execution stack (line 483) vs 5.0 rerun rules (lines 503-509) and step 0.3 label table
verified.claim: The stack requirement is not enforced before any value is computed. Its suggested remedy, 'moving onto the recorded stack', is called a code-only fix, which does not fit 5.0's rerun rules.
verified.evidence: Line 481 says the actor 'runs under the rerun1 runtime receipt... The receipt is recorded'. It never says the receipt is asserted before the 4.8 values are computed. Line 483 then gives 'moving onto the recorded stack' as the example code-only fix, which assumes a first attempt could run on a different stack. 5.0 defines a code-only fix as a recorded and approved diff (line 506-507). A change of environment has no code diff. Under 5.0's second-failure rule ('under code unchanged since that unit's previous attempt', line 509), a rerun after a stack-only move still counts as running unchanged code. So it is unclear whether the move uses up the unit's one fix or simply leaves the next failure to end the step INCONCLUSIVE. 5.0's protection for sealed units also covers code only. The other step 0.3 units on the same critics (G0.5, edge slopes, onset contrast) may have been sealed on the old stack. In rerun1 the receipt is enforced inside runtime.create (runtime.py 112 and 571, which call runtime_receipt and raise 'Frozen runtime versions differ'). A new evaluator gets that enforcement only if it builds the policy through that path.
verified.fix: In 4.8, require the receipt to be asserted (runtime_receipt, or equality with the recorded receipt) before any reproduction value is computed. A failed assertion is then an execution failure (INCOMPLETE) with no values produced. Then either say that a stack correction is an environment fix, recorded and approved with the rerun, that does not count as the unit's code-only fix, or say explicitly that it counts as that fix and that a later failure ends the step INCONCLUSIVE. Drop the bare example 'such as moving onto the recorded stack'.

check.reason: Partly refuted. Line 481 cites runtime.py runtime_receipt 47-59, and that function is nothing but require() assertions (56: 'Frozen runtime versions differ'; 57-58: GPU/JIT/x64 off; 59: matmul 'highest'). Rerun1 calls it before any computation (runtime.py 112 in create, 571). So 'runs under the receipt' already reads as asserted. What is left is a real inconsistency in wording only. Line 483's example fix, 'moving onto the recorded stack', is not a 'code-only fix' under 5.0 (lines 506-507 require a recorded and approved diff). 5.0's sealed-unit protection and second-failure clause ('code unchanged', line 509) speak only of code, so it is unclear whether a stack move uses up the unit's one fix. This fails closed. A rerun after a stack-only move that fails again is 'code unchanged', so the step becomes INCONCLUSIVE. An off-stack run with values inside 1e-9 still shows the evaluator is correct. No false pass and no threshold change can come from it. The fix is a cheap rewording: say the receipt is asserted (runtime_receipt raises) before any 4.8 value, so a stack mismatch is an execution INCOMPLETE with no values; drop the bare example, or say whether a stack correction counts as the unit's fix. This does not block A1.

verified.claim: The cited receipt does not pin everything the 143/143 evidence depended on. It omits seven of the 11 pinned packages and the device kind, gives a short line span, and does not name the runtime environment the check needs.
verified.evidence: runtime.py 51-56 pins 11 packages: jax, jaxlib, jax-cuda12-plugin and jax-cuda12-pjrt at 0.6.2, plus numpy 2.5.4, flax 0.10.7, optax 0.2.8, distrax 0.1.5, chex 0.1.90, tensorflow-probability 0.25.0 and scipy 1.18.1. The draft names only the four JAX ones, yet distrax and TFP run the .sample(seed=None) path. The function is defined at lines 47-63; its checks end at 59. runtime_receipt does not assert the device. The recorded receipts (run/evaluation/report.json runtime_receipts, 9 cells, all identical) show 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU', executable /home/david/bca-operator-audit-20261026/bin/python (WSL) and Python 3.12.14. The 143/143 Tier-1 match was same code, same device, same environment, run to run (continuation1 attempt against rerun1). Neither receipt pins the CUDA math libraries or the driver. JAX's GPU backend with the cuda12 plugins runs in that WSL environment, not in the native Windows .venv. No conflict with the training runtime was found: Part 4's host configuration pins only f2dc1278, which matches the rerun1 upstream provenance f2dc1278eae1.
verified.fix: Cite the recorded receipt (run/evaluation/report.json runtime_receipts) as well as runtime.py 47-63. Require equality of the full package dict, the backend and flags, and device_kinds. Name the environment the 4.8 check runs in. Optionally add that a mismatch traced only to library or device differences should be diagnosed before the single fix is used.

check.reason: Refuted on its main points. (1) The draft does not leave out seven packages. It cites the function runtime_receipt, and that function asserts the full 11-package dict (runtime.py 51-56: numpy 2.5.4, flax 0.10.7, optax 0.2.8, distrax 0.1.5, chex 0.1.90, tfp 0.25.0, scipy 1.18.1, along with the four JAX packages). The prose list at line 481 is a summary of a citation that pins them all. (2) The line span is right: 47-59 covers every assertion (56, 57-58, 59), and 60-63 is only the return dict. (3) Device kind and environment are true facts but do not affect validity. The recorded receipts (run/evaluation/report.json, 9 cells, all identical) show RTX 5070 Ti, the WSL python, 3.12.14 and the identical 11-package dict. Zeus is the only host and has one GPU. On the native Windows .venv, runtime_receipt's 'gpu' backend check (line 57) or the jax-cuda12 version lookup would raise, and a different device that changed float32 bits would show up as a Q^pi mismatch, which is INCOMPLETE (line 483). Both fail closed, and neither can produce a false pass. The 143/143 figure checks out (RUN_RESULT.json reproduction.tier1_exact = 143, contexts_checked 144, tier2 deviation 0.0). Optionally, 4.8 could also cite report.json runtime_receipts and name the WSL environment. That would be a clarity gain, not a validity fix.

checked_ok: continuation_values (reference.py 242-276) is called once per (snapshot, context) bank with 32 anchors x 6 slots = 192 rows. CONTEXTS = ('ordinary','strong_current') at evaluation.py:21, the call is at evaluation.py:437, and the per-bank loop is evaluate_worker.py 602-604. 9 cells x 2 = 18 calls; run/evaluation holds exactly 18 *__native__20000__*.json files, each with 32 per_probe rows.

Offset 0 makes no actor call: reference.py 265-266 uses first[active], built by deployed_actions on the bank. Offsets >= 1 call actor_actions on the active rows in the original order (lines 267-269). The loop spans 259-272 as cited.
require(1 <= n <= 64) at reference.py:254, so a merged 64-anchor call would be accepted, as the draft says.

evaluate_worker.py:351 is FrozenPolicy._act = jax.jit(lambda obs: actor.apply_fn(actor.params,obs).sample(seed=None)). reference.actor_actions (115-130) calls policy.act, which calls self._act, so it is the function used during the continuation.

runtime.py runtime_receipt begins at line 47. Lines 51-59 assert jax, jaxlib and both cuda12 packages at 0.6.2, a GPU backend, JIT on, x64 off and matmul precision 'highest'. The recorded receipts for all 9 cells in run/evaluation/report.json are identical.

RUN_RESULT.json reproduction: tier1_exact = 143, recorded_contexts = 143, tier2_near_exact = 0, largest_tier2_scaled_deviation = 0.0. The only new context is seed2_random__distance__20000/strong_current, so all 18 native 20k contexts were reproduced byte-identically.

Canonical dynamics() does not depend on batch shape (fixed summation order, thrusterchain.py 201-219), so the float64 states, and with them the actor inputs, repeat bit for bit across batch layouts. reference.observation's float32 remaining-time encoding gives the same bits as float32-division and 1-t/H variants for all t in 0..100 (scratch check).
The claim that 1e-9 absorbs only float64 summation order holds once the states and float32 actions repeat.
The new training runtime does not conflict with the pin: Part 4's host configuration pins Unifloral f2dc1278, and rerun1's provenance is f2dc1278eae18ed3e22c92255119c54885414d17.

The step 0.4 forecast base set (valid anchors under each continuation, non-predictor-valid ones as minus infinity) is consistent with V0(d)'s base set (valid in every arm compared), with Part 2 line 200 and with Part 8.2 line 877. The (50-k)/(100-k) quantile was confirmed by simulation: 0.444 at k = 10 and 0.455 at 4/48.
The line 668 median rule holds: with item 5 at >= 90% of 48 anchors there are at most 4 minus-infinity entries, below middle positions 24 and 25.
Spot-checked numbers outside this lens's focus: 0.5 x 0.65 - 0.15 = 0.175. In the 48-anchor example, K1a = 0.45 and the recomputed value is 0.50, so the reading is withheld.
'At most one code-only fix per unit before the rerun' matches 5.0's wording (line 506), and the step 0.3 table's 'Fix the evaluator, then a fresh A2' matches the fresh-approval requirement.

No r11 sentence changes a threshold, label or label precedence. The K1a and K1c rows, V0(a)-(e), the label tables and readings 1-6 keep the same logic. The one approval-adjacent wording is the stack-move-as-code-only-fix example (P11-1).

packed.verdict: r11 fixes all 11 items from VERIFY_CRITIC_DIGEST_r10 in the text itself, not only in the Review 11 table. I found no new gate threshold, label, precedence or approval-rule change. Every numeric claim I recomputed holds. The relative-clause margin is 0.5M - 0.15 = 0.175 at M = 0.65, and the absolute-clause margin is 0. The 48-anchor example gives K1a 0.45, median KC_C 0.45 and recomputed K1a exactly 0.50 in both float64 and float32, so the strict '< +0.5' withholds the reading. The simulation reproduces at 0.222 and 0.616, against 0.22 and 0.61 in VERIFY_WORKFLOW_r10.json. Minus-infinity entries are at most floor(0.1N), which is 3-4 for N = 32-48, so they never reach the middle positions. All 41 Part 11 hashes match. The source citations check out: evaluate_worker.py:351, runtime.py:47-59, evaluation.py:21 and :437, reference.py:259-272, and RUN_RESULT tier1_exact = 143 of 143 recorded contexts. None of the listed stale phrases survives outside history rows. What remains is all low and all fail-closed or wording. (1) The new 4.8 example calls 'moving onto the recorded stack' a code-only fix. That stretches 5.0's rule, and it sits awkwardly with Review 11's claim that no approval rule changed. (2) The pinned stack leaves out the GPU model. The receipt records it (RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU) but does not require it. (3) Review 10 rows 7 and 8 and Review 9's row-12 note are superseded by r11 but carry no annotation. (4) The new K1c noise wording leaves out 'in every seed' in Part 2, overstates 'this gives a FAIL' in 8.2(iii), uses M before it is defined, and adds no caveat at reading 1. (5) 4.5's 'therefore repeat' is unhedged, and 4.5 never defines the batch. (6) There are smaller scope, citation and count slips. None of these affects a label or opens a false-PASS or wrong-reading path. r11 remains ready for A1 consideration, and a short text-only pass would close these points.

low_findings.section: 4.8 Batching and execution stack (line 483); Review 11 row 1 (line 1203) and preamble (line 1199)
low_findings.claim: The new sentence 'Like any INCOMPLETE, it allows at most one code-only fix before the rerun, such as moving onto the recorded stack (5.0)' treats a change of runtime environment as 5.0's 'code-only fix'. 5.0 does not define that. Review 11 then says no approval rule changed.
low_findings.evidence: 5.0 (lines 506-508) allows 'At most one code-only fix per unit'. It requires that 'the diff is recorded and approved with the rerun' and that 'the diff must leave untouched the code that produced already-sealed units'. Both conditions describe a code diff, not a change of package versions or GPU backend. 4.8 line 481 already makes the recorded stack mandatory ('It runs under the rerun1 runtime receipt'), and runtime_receipt require()s the versions, GPU and JIT on, x64 off and 'highest' precision (runtime.py 54-59). So a run off that stack breaks the protocol before any value is compared. Calling the recovery a 'code-only fix' spends the unit's single fix on a non-code change, or else silently widens 5.0. Review 11 row 1 repeats it as 'a mismatch takes 5.0's one code-only fix'.
low_findings.fix: Replace the clause with: 'A run that is not on the recorded stack fails its receipt and is INCOMPLETE. The rerun on the recorded stack with unchanged code is the ordinary rerun (fresh approval) and does not use the unit's code-only fix.' Alternatively, amend 5.0 to say explicitly that an environment-only correction to a pinned receipt counts as the code-only fix. Align Review 11 row 1.

low_findings.claim: 'On that stack the float32 actions are expected to repeat bit for bit' rests on rerun1's 143/143 reproduction, but the pinned 'stack' leaves out the GPU model. runtime_receipt records device_kinds without requiring it.
low_findings.evidence: runtime.py:61 records 'device_kinds' in the returned dict, but no require() checks it (lines 54-59 check only versions, backend, JIT, x64 and precision). run/evaluation/report.json records a single device kind for every cell: 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU'. XLA/cuBLAS kernel selection can differ across GPU architectures under identical versions, so a user run of 4.8 on another GPU could miss 1e-9 with no real fault. This fails closed (INCOMPLETE, then possibly INCONCLUSIVE). It narrows the r10 digest item 1 fix rather than leaving it open.
low_findings.fix: Add the device kind to the pinned stack: 'on the recorded device kind (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU, run/evaluation/report.json), asserted in the receipt'. Or say that the bit-for-bit expectation holds only on that device.

low_findings.section: Part 9 history: Review 10 table rows 7-8 (lines 1180-1181), Review 9 note row 12 (line 1154), note after Review 10 table (lines 1186-1189)
low_findings.claim: r11 supersedes three more history statements but does not annotate them, which is the same bookkeeping gap the r10 digest item 3 asked to close. The lens-name correction was also made in place, while the note says only 'Three' of Review 10's statements were corrected.
low_findings.evidence: Review 10 row 7 still says the step 0.4 forecast is 'over the 48 gated anchors'; r11 line 608 changed the base set to the anchors valid under each continuation. Review 10 row 8 and the Review 9 note row 12 still say 'noise-driven misses fall under the joint statement'; r11 line 212 routes K1c noise misses to FAIL plus reading 1, not to the joint statement. The note at 1186-1189 lists only row 10, row 11 and the 'everything else' sentence. Line 1156's '(logic, resolution)' was edited in place, so the history text now differs from what Review 10 originally recorded, with no annotation. Review 11 row 3 says 'Corrected or annotated'.
low_findings.fix: Extend the note after the Review 10 table with 'row 7: base set refined in revision 11 to the anchors valid under each continuation' and 'row 8: for K1c, noise-driven misses are FAIL with reading 1 (revision 11, Part 2 Noise)'. Add '(refined in revision 11 for K1c)' to the Review 9 note row 12. Either say 'Four statements' and list the lens names, or note that the lens names were corrected in place.

low_findings.claim: The new K1c noise wording has four problems. It is inconsistent about when reading 1 attaches. It overstates when noise causes a FAIL. It uses M before defining it. It leaves reading 1 itself without the caveat, although reading 2 got one.
low_findings.evidence: Line 212: 'For K1c, it is a FAIL, and reading 1 then describes the measured critic'. Reading 1 attaches only to FAIL-consistent (lines 522, 724), and line 884 correctly says 'in every seed it gives reading 1'. Line 884: 'For K1c this gives a FAIL', where 'this' is falling below rho_hat_C - tol 'at some anchors' (line 883). That causes a FAIL only if the median drops below the bar. Line 212 uses 'M' ('0.5 M - 0.15'), but M is first defined at line 216 ('the C-valid median M of rho_hat_C(s10)'). Reading 1 (725) still states flatly 'this Unifloral critic does not over-value', while reading 2 gained a conservatism pointer (730). At the gate edge the absolute-clause margin is 0, so a critic that is correct on average can get reading 1. Line 903 treats exactly that outcome, reading 1 on 'a critic that over-values by about the true gap', as a defect worth a user decision.
low_findings.fix: Line 212: 'For K1c, a miss caused by such noise is a FAIL; if it occurs in every seed, reading 1 then describes the measured critic, noise included', and define M inline ('the C-valid median M of rho_hat_C(s10)'). Line 884: 'For K1c, if it pushes the median below a bar, this gives a FAIL...'. Reading 1: add '(the measured critic, CUTOFF KC noise included; Part 2, Noise)'.

low_findings.claim: The new 4.5 bullet says 'Their float32 actions therefore repeat' without the hedge that 4.8 now uses ('expected to repeat'). The conclusion also does not quite follow when each evaluator builds its own observations. The batch it pins, 'the anchor bank', is undefined in step 0.4.
low_findings.evidence: Each evaluator 'builds its own observations' from float64 states that may differ by float64 summation order, which is exactly what 1e-9 is meant to absorb. A ULP-level float64 difference can occasionally round a float32 observation differently, change an action, and compound over the continuation. 'Bank' is defined (line 49) as a set of starts, but the 4.5 check runs at 'every step 0.4 anchor, at three slots (-KNEE, s10, s20), in all three worlds' (64 E2 + 32 E1 anchors at four times). It is unclear whether the batch is all probe slots or the three checked slots, and whether E1 and E2 are batched together. Both evaluators must make the same choice, so the risk is again fail-closed (INCOMPLETE at step 0.4, line 617).
low_findings.fix: Write 'are expected to repeat' and define the batch, for example 'all active rows of the (anchor set, world) probe batch at each offset, the same rows and slots in both evaluators'. Optionally add that a mismatch traced only to float32 observation rounding is diagnosed as such.

low_findings.claim: r11 states in the same bullet group that offset 0 makes no actor call, but keeps 'a Q^pi row compounds up to 100 actor calls'. The true maximum is 99.
low_findings.evidence: reference.py continuation_values: remaining = HORIZON - times, with a maximum of 100 at t = 0. The loop runs offsets 0..99, and actor_actions is called only for offset >= 1 (lines 263-268). That is at most 99 actor calls per row. Line 480 now says 'offset >= 1 (offset 0 takes the bank's first action, with no actor call)'.

low_findings.claim: The even-count rule is scoped to 'Every median in Stage 1'. Two other medians are left without it: the step 0.4 forecast medians, which also use minus infinity, and the Stage 2 repair-screen medians that r11 just tied to 'Stage 1's definition'.
low_findings.evidence: Line 608: the step 0.4 forecast takes medians over the valid gated anchors (up to 48, an even count) with minus-infinity entries. Line 806: the Stage 2 screen takes medians over 'the Stage 2 common gated anchors (Stage 1's definition applied to the Stage 2 arms)', which carries over the anchor-set definition, not the median rule. The minus-infinity bound in the Medians bullet relies on Stage 1's V0(d) item 5 at 90%. Step 0.4 has the same 90% rule (item 5, line 184), so the bound would hold there too, but nothing says so.
low_findings.fix: Change to 'Every median in this protocol (step 0.4's forecast, Stage 1 and Stage 2) ... For an even count it is the average of the two middle values'. Optionally note that step 0.4's item 5 at 90% gives the same minus-infinity bound.

Part 11 lists only runtime.py make_adapter, context and heldout refresh, and data.py, for rerun1. critic.verdict:
Revision 11 is ready for A1 consideration. I recommend one wording fix before the user reads it. No high item remains, and the single medium item is an approval-adjacent wording problem that fails closed.

Ruling (1), on whether r11 changed any threshold, label, precedence or approval rule. It changed no threshold, label or precedence. The K1a and K1c rows, V0(a)-(e), the label tables, readings 1-6 and the precedence order keep the same logic, and both lenses checked the full diff against the declared hunks. One sentence touches an approval rule. Line 483 gives "moving onto the recorded stack" as an example of 5.0's "one code-only fix". 5.0 (lines 506-509) defines that fix as a recorded and approved code diff, and its rule for a second failure turns on whether the code is unchanged. A change of environment is not a code diff, so the example quietly stretches 5.0. Review 11 (lines 1199, 1203) then says no approval rule changed. This fails closed and cannot produce a false pass, but the wording should be repaired.

Ruling (2), on whether the 4.8 and 4.5 procedural pins are correct and feasible. They are correct. I re-checked the following against the source:
- continuation_values (reference.py 242-276) runs offsets 0..max(remaining)-1. Offset 0 takes first[active] and makes no actor call. Offsets of 1 or more call actor_actions on the active rows in order. The cap is require(1 <= n <= 64) at line 254.
- The per-bank loop is at evaluate_worker.py 602-604, with two contexts per cell. That gives 18 calls and 18 native__20000 JSONs.
- FrozenPolicy._act at evaluate_worker.py 351 is jax.jit(lambda obs: actor.apply_fn(actor.params, obs).sample(seed=None)), with the parameters captured by the closure.
- runtime_receipt at runtime.py 47-59 asserts all 11 package pins, a GPU backend, JIT on, x64 off and matmul precision 'highest'. It records device_kinds but does not assert them.
- RUN_RESULT.json gives reproduction.tier1_exact = 143 of 143 recorded contexts.
- Canonical dynamics() does not depend on batch shape.

The pins are feasible only in the recorded WSL GPU environment. On the native Windows .venv the receipt would raise, which fails closed. Three weaknesses are wording only:
- 4.5's "same batch: all active rows of the anchor bank" is undefined for step 0.4. The cross-check runs at three slots, while the main evaluator covers many slots over 64 E2 and 32 E1 anchors.
- "Therefore repeat" in 4.5 is not hedged, while 4.8 says "expected to repeat".
- 4.5 does not say the shared function is only the raw actor forward pass. If the ±KNEE clip were shared, a clip error would be common to both evaluators and go uncaught.

Ruling (3), on whether the round-10 items are resolved. All 11 items in VERIFY_CRITIC_DIGEST_r10 are resolved in the protocol text itself, not only in the Review 11 table. I re-checked the following:
- The 0.5M - 0.15 = 0.175 margin.
- The 48-anchor example: the recomputed value is exactly 0.50, so the reading is withheld.
- The simulation: 0.222 and 0.616, reported as 0.22 and 0.61.
- The (50-k)/(100-k) quantile: 0.444 at k = 10.
- The minus-infinity bound: at most 4 of 48 entries.
- All 41 Part 11 hashes.

r11 itself leaves new bookkeeping gaps. Review 10 rows 7 and 8, and the row 12 note under Review 9, are superseded by r11 but carry no annotation. One small correction in that note is also inaccurate.

Findings I dropped:
- P11-2's main claims are refuted. runtime_receipt asserts all 11 packages, and lines 47-59 cover every assertion.
- P11-1 is downgraded from "never asserted". The cited function consists entirely of require() checks, and rerun1 calls it before any computation.

must_fix.section: 4.8 Batching and execution stack (line 483); 5.0 (lines 503-509); Review 11 preamble and row 1 (lines 1199, 1203)
must_fix.issue: The example 'such as moving onto the recorded stack' calls a change of runtime environment 5.0's 'code-only fix'. 5.0 defines that fix as a recorded and approved code diff, and its sealed-unit and second-failure clauses speak only of code. So it is unclear whether a stack move uses up the unit's one fix. A rerun after a stack-only move counts as 'code unchanged', so a second failure ends the step INCONCLUSIVE. Review 11 also says no approval rule changed. The text never says the receipt is checked before any 4.8 value is computed, though rerun1 does check it first (runtime.py 112, 571).
must_fix.fix: In 4.8, write: 'runtime_receipt (or equality with the recorded receipt) is asserted before any reproduction value is computed. A failed assertion is an execution INCOMPLETE with no values produced. The rerun on the recorded stack with unchanged code is the ordinary fresh-approval rerun and does not use the unit's code-only fix.' Delete the 'such as moving onto the recorded stack' example. In Review 11 row 1, replace 'a mismatch takes 5.0's one code-only fix' with matching wording.

must_fix.issue: Three problems. (a) 'The same batch: all active rows of the anchor bank' is undefined for step 0.4. Line 49 defines 'bank' as a set of starts. The cross-check runs at three slots, while the main evaluator covers S9, s05, s10, s15, s20, p10 and the T-images over 64 E2 and 32 E1 anchors. If the layouts differ, the check fails closed. If the main evaluator is rerun with a matching layout, the check verifies the rerun rather than the gated values. (b) 'Therefore repeat' is not hedged, and each evaluator builds its own float32 observations from float64 states. (c) It does not say the shared function is only the raw forward pass. If the ±KNEE clip, the deployed-action handling or the actor binding were shared, an error in them would be common to both evaluators and go uncaught.
must_fix.fix: Write: 'Both call the same raw actor forward pass (no clipping), on the main evaluator's own batch layout for the gated values: all forced slots of the named anchor set, per world and continuation seed, in its row order. The raw loop reproduces that full layout and is compared at the three named slots. Their float32 actions are expected to repeat. Each evaluator applies the ±KNEE clip itself and checks the actor's identity (parameter digest against the frozen cell) separately.'

must_fix.issue: The new K1c noise wording has four problems. Line 212 attaches reading 1 to any K1c FAIL, but reading 1 requires FAIL in every seed. Line 884's 'For K1c this gives a FAIL' overstates, because noise below rho_hat_C - tol 'at some anchors' gives a FAIL only if it moves a median below its bar. M is used at line 212 but first defined at line 216. Reading 1 gets no caveat, although reading 2 got one at line 730.
must_fix.fix: Line 212: 'For K1c, a miss caused by such noise is a FAIL; if it occurs in every seed, reading 1 then describes the measured critic, noise included', and define M inline. Line 884: 'if it pushes a median below its bar, this gives a FAIL'. Reading 1: add '(the measured critic, CUTOFF KC noise included; Part 2, Noise)'.

must_fix.section: Part 9: Review 10 rows 7-8 (lines 1180-1181), Review 9 note row 12 (~line 1154), note after the Review 10 table (lines 1186-1189)
must_fix.issue: r11 supersedes Review 10 row 7 (the base set is now the anchors valid under each continuation, line 608). It also supersedes row 8 and the Review 9 row 12 note (K1c noise misses are now FAIL with reading 1, not the joint statement). None of these is annotated. The note says 'Three' statements were corrected, though the lens names at 1156 were also edited in place. Its row 10 correction says 4.5b cites authenticate_core 36-61 'only', but 4.5b also cites line 151 and _dynamics 198-199.
must_fix.fix: Add 'row 7: base set refined in revision 11 to the anchors valid under each continuation' and 'row 8: for K1c, noise-driven misses are FAIL with reading 1 (revision 11)'. Add '(refined in revision 11 for K1c)' to the Review 9 row 12 note. Say the lens names were corrected in place. Reword row 10 as '4.5b cites authenticate_core 36-61, line 151 and _dynamics 198-199, not actor_actions'.

must_fix.issue: The pin leaves out three facts a reimplementation needs to repeat bit for bit. The actor parameters are closed over as constants in a jit compiled per policy, so jitting apply_fn with traced params is a different XLA program. The policy is built through runtime.branch, then restore_snapshot, then FrozenPolicy (evaluate_worker.py 600-601). The receipt does not assert the device kind, which is recorded as NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU in run/evaluation/report.json, and it runs only in the WSL environment. The 'once per bank' citation (evaluation.py 21, 437) also omits the per-bank loop.
must_fix.fix: Require actions to come from rerun1's FrozenPolicy (evaluate_worker.py 344-358) built on the state restore_snapshot returns, or state the closure-constant form exactly. Add evaluate_worker.py 602-604 to the batch citation. Also cite the recorded receipts (run/evaluation/report.json runtime_receipts), name the WSL runtime environment, and either require the recorded device kind or limit the bit-for-bit expectation to it.

must_fix.issue: 'Stage 1's definition applied to the Stage 2 arms' does not say which branches must be valid, or whether it means the 48 gated fresh-evaluation anchors or the detection anchors. It is reported only.
must_fix.fix: Write 'over the 48 gated Stage 2 evaluation anchors valid under both the BCA and the native-replicate branches' own clipped continuations in stall CUTOFF, per seed', and report the count.

must_fix.issue: The forecast now excludes invalid anchors but reports neither the base-set size nor the minus-infinity count. The rule for an even count (average the two middle values) is scoped to 'Every median in Stage 1', which leaves out the step 0.4 forecast and the Stage 2 screen medians.
must_fix.fix: Report the valid-anchor count and the minus-infinity count per continuation seed next to the two forecast medians. Change line 668 to 'Every median in this protocol (step 0.4's forecast, Stage 1 and Stage 2)'.

must_fix.issue: 'A Q^pi row compounds up to 100 actor calls' should say 99. remaining is at most 100, and actor calls happen only at offsets 1..99 (reference.py 259-268), which r11 itself states at line 480. Part 11's code-facts list also leaves out r11's new citations.
must_fix.fix: Change to 'up to 99 actor calls'. Add to Part 11: evaluate_worker.py 351 and 602-604, runtime.py 47-59, evaluation.py 21 and 437, and RUN_RESULT.json reproduction.tier1_exact 143 of 143.

residual_risks: The 4.8 known-answer reproduction works only in the recorded WSL GPU setup: the same 11 package versions, very likely the same GPU model, and the actor rebuilt through rerun1's own FrozenPolicy path. Run anywhere else, it stops as INCOMPLETE. A second failure under unchanged code ends step 0.3 INCONCLUSIVE, even if the evaluator is correct.

The 4.5 cross-check now shares the actor function between the two evaluators. If more than the raw network call is shared (for example the ±KNEE clip or the choice of checkpoint), an error there appears in both evaluators and the check cannot catch it. Only the observations and remaining time are checked independently.

The reachability forecast is still borderline: the clipped-LQR proxy gives rho(s05) of about 0.61 against a level of about 0.6. r11 changes only how the forecast is reported, so a Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE from V0(d) remains a realistic outcome.

At the gate edge, K1c's absolute clause has no margin for CUTOFF critic noise. A critic that is correct on average can therefore fail K1c and get reading 1. This is disclosed and costs power, not label validity.
Learner competence is still unproven. The pins guarantee that the evaluators reproduce recorded values, not that the new Stage 1 models will learn the knee.
Small history and bookkeeping errors in Part 9 could confuse a later reviewer about which earlier resolutions still stand, though none of them changes a gate.
